_doc: Original text for the natural landmarks and vignettes: who lies where, what they wrote, and what the land is called. Epitaph lines must be 15 characters or fewer (one sign line). Placeholders in notes: {name} {other} {place} {trade} {cause} {weather} {item} {dir} {thing}. Names come from NpcNames by the province's folk (races), so every culture sounds like itself.
causes: a wrong turn in the dark

grave: To {name}, {trade}. {other} dug this grave in {weather} and could not find a priest. Whoever you are, leave the stones as they lie. Taken by {cause}.
Here we put {name}. Not the finest of us, not the worst. {cause} took what it took. {other} will come back in spring with a proper marker, if the road lets her.
{name} asked to be buried where she could hear the water. It is not far. {other} carried the stones up one at a time and said the words as best he could.
I never knew your name, traveller, so I gave you {name}. You had {item} in your hand. I left it with you. {other}, passing through.
{name}, {trade}, died of {cause} three days from the nearest roof. We stayed with the body one night. We did not sleep. Please do not disturb the stones.
My brother {name} rests here. He was a {trade} and never harmed anyone who did not ask for it. If you are a decent person, say his name once and go on.
traveller: Day nine, and the pack is lighter every morning. {weather} all night. I keep to the {dir} ridge and talk to myself so I remember what a voice sounds like. If {other} finds this, tell her I tried.
I lost the road for a day. Found it again by luck near {place}. The water here is fit to drink; the ground to the {dir} is not. I marked it with three stones.
Slept badly. Something walked around the camp twice in the dark and did not touch a thing. In the morning there were no prints. I am leaving this note, and the fire cold, and going on at first light.
To whoever finds this: I was a {trade} and I owed {other} a debt. If I do not return, the {item} under the rock is yours. Please do not tell {other} where I went.
The pass was closed by {weather}, so I waited. Three days is a long time with only my thoughts. I counted every stone in the cairn. There are forty-one. Do not move them.
The map I bought is wrong. The river is not where it says. I have been walking {dir} since the morning and I have seen nothing but {weather}. If you are reading this you are lost, too.
hunter: A good stag, four days from the hold. {other} and I took him at dusk and dressed him here. We left the head for whatever the land wants. Do not take the hide from the rack; it is ours.
Tracks lead {dir} from here, big, deeper than a bear's. {name} would not follow them. I have never seen him afraid. We are leaving the traps and going home.
Rule of this place: leave dry wood for the next hunter, leave the fire laid, and take only what you eat. {name}, {trade}, first of the camp.
Season's tally: eleven deer, two boar, one elk the size of a cart. {other} claims it was twelve. Writing it down so we stop arguing. {weather} tomorrow, by the smell of it.
smuggler: Drop is behind the loose stone. Two barrels, one crate. Do not touch the crate. Leave the coin in the pot and be gone by dawn. - {name}
The watch came through at {weather} and did not look hard. We moved the stock to the {dir} cave. If you are the buyer, the price is the same as before, and not a copper less.
To {other}: you were told twice not to carry it past {place}. Whatever happens now is yours. I have a boat and a long way to be. - {name}
Three signs of safe drop: a stone on the sign, a cloth on the post, a knot in the line. If any is missing, go away and do not return for a month.
ghost: The house was empty before {name} came to it. People say he bought it cheap because no one else would stay past midnight. He stayed. Now no one says if he left.
They say {name} still tends the hearth. The ash is always warm, though no one has lit it in years. Do not take anything from the table. Do not answer if it asks your name.
A traveller slept here in {weather} and woke to find his boots set neatly by the door and a cup of water by his hand. He did not stay for breakfast. He did leave a coin.
Whatever lives here is not cruel. It only wants the door shut and the light kept low. A lamp left burning will be found out in the morning, and the oil topped up.
pilgrim: I came this way to give thanks. The shrine is old and small and no one tends it, so I have swept it and set flowers. If you pass, say a word for {name}, who is why I came.
Four days of walking to kneel for a minute. Worth it. The stone is warm, even in {weather}. I left {item} on the ledge. I think it will be gone by morning. I hope so.
Every year I come. Every year there is a little more moss and a little less paint on the face of the stone. Next year I will bring a brush. The year after, the family.
The old priest said it is not the gods who need the shrine, but we, and so we build one wherever we have to stand still. I stand still here. - {name}
scholar: Measured the stones today. Eleven stand, four are fallen, one is missing. The missing one is not in the field. Someone took it with care. {other} thinks a mason. I think a person who wanted to be remembered.
Rubbing taken from the east face. The glyphs are old and not Nordic; not Ayleid; not anything I have in the books. Left a copy under the cairn for the next scholar. - {name}

The dig has yielded a bone comb, {item}, and a layer of ash older than the road. The ash is from a fire so big that nothing grew after. Add that to the list of things we do not discuss at the college.
Dated the strata: the grave is older than the stone, the stone is older than the road, and the road is older than whatever the locals say is the oldest thing here. Humility, everyone.
hermit: I came here to be alone, and I have been. It is quieter than I expected and louder than I deserve. The goat is good company; she judges me only when I deserve it.
Visitors: one this year. A girl who wanted to know the way. I told her. She did not say thanks. I took it as a compliment; manners are for people with company.
Rules of the house: knock if you must, leave a coin if you take bread, do not touch the third shelf. The third shelf is where I keep the old letters.
ambush: The cart was loaded for market: wool, salt, a small cask of something strong. We were three hours from {place} when the arrows came. I write this with the shaft still in my arm. Do not follow the road.
They took the horses, the coin, and the boots from the dead. Not the cargo. That means they will come back for it with a wagon. Take what you can carry and go.
{name} put himself between the cart and the road. It did not help, but it was a good thing to do. I am leaving this note on his chest so someone knows.
miner: The timbers groaned all night. {name} says it is only {weather} on the hill, but I have worked {trade} long enough to know a roof that is thinking about falling. We shore up the {dir} gallery at first light.

Third collapse this month. {other} is on the wrong side of it and we can hear him tapping. Two taps, a pause, two taps. We dig. The lamp oil is low. If this log is found, the vein ran {dir}, not down.
Day four behind the fall. Water drips from the {dir} wall and we drink it. {other} has stopped answering. I have {item} and a little light. Tell the foreman the adit was sound until it was not.

Excavation log. The brass wall gave way today and behind it, a hall of Dwemer make, dry and cold and humming faintly. {other} swears the pipes moved. We have tagged {item} and sealed the door. Nobody goes below until the surveyor returns.
overlook: Sat here an hour and said nothing, which is a record for me. The land runs out {dir} further than any map admits, and {weather} is drifting across it like a slow thought. Worth every blister. - {name}
Climbed up in {weather} for this view and was rewarded with fog. Stayed anyway. Around noon it tore open like a curtain and I forgot my feet entirely. Carve your name if you like, but look first.
The bench is old and someone has kept it mended. I do not know who, and I would like to thank them. I leave {item} beneath it as payment. {place} is just visible to the {dir}, small as a coin.
explorer: Day twelve. Camp on the ice-shelf, three days past the last cairn. {weather} has not let up. Rations fine. Spirits fine. Fingers less so. We go {dir} at first light and hope for a pass.
Day nineteen. {other} is gone, taken by {cause}. We could not recover him. Cold now. Wrote this with a stub of lead. Ink froze. Going {dir}.
Day twenty-three. No fire. Fuel out. Can hear nothing. Wrote name here so someone knows. {name}, {trade}. Tired. So tired. The snow looks soft.
castaway: Day 1. Washed ashore with {item} and the clothes I wore. {weather} all night. Found fresh water in the rocks to the {dir}. Alive. That is all I will say today.
Day 14. Cut a notch for each sunrise on the driftwood post. Eaten shellfish until I dream of bread. Saw a sail once, far off. I waved until my arms failed. It did not turn.
Day 31. Stopped counting for a while, then started again, because counting is the only thing that is mine. If you land here, the spring is {dir} of the tall rock. Please take the post with you.
angler: Catch book. Two pike, one carp the length of my arm, and a boot. The boot is not counted. {weather}, light wind, water dark. Good day. Never fish from the {dir} bank after dusk; I do not say why.
Slow week. {other} swears the fish bite on the turn of the tide, and the old fools may be right. Three trout, a perch, a lost line. {weather} tomorrow, so I will stay in and mend nets.
A true angler spits on the first fish and puts it back. I forgot once, and caught nothing till the next moon. I do not believe in luck. I do it anyway. - {name}
cabin: Garden is in at last. Turnips, leeks, a row of cabbages the deer will eat. {weather} nearly spoiled the beans, but the hearth dried the seed-box. I talk to the hens now. They are poor conversation and good company.

Cut wood for the winter and stacked it to the eaves. The chimney draws well when the wind sits in the {dir}. {name} once sat by this fire, a long time ago, and never said where she was going. I left the chair as it was.
The old ones say a barrow lies a half-day {dir} of here, and that lights walk it in {weather}. I have never gone. A person who lives alone learns what to leave undisturbed.
Found {item} in the creek bed after the thaw. Very old, very fine, not mine. I have put it on the high shelf. If someone comes for it, they may have it, with my blessing and a bowl of stew.
herbalist: Gathered at dawn: nightshade by the {dir} wall, moss from the north side of the oaks, a handful of bright flowers that smell of rain. Dry them all in shade. Never sun. Never.
Avoid the pale caps by the water. They look gentle and they are not. {other} ate one on a dare and slept three days. The red berries are worse, and they are everywhere. Taste nothing you cannot name.
Good ground, this. Healing moss, thistle, and a stubborn creeping root that knits a wound faster than any priest. Take half of what you find and leave the rest to seed. - {name}, {trade}
beekeeper: Six hives, strong. The queens are laying and the clover is out. I check the boxes at midday when the bees are busy. {weather} is a bad omen for the honey, but good for my patience.
Told the bees of {name}'s passing, as the old custom asks. I knocked on each hive and whispered. They hummed lower for a day. Perhaps they only heard the wind. Perhaps not.
The best honey comes from the flowers on the {dir} slope, wild and sharp and golden. Do not wear dark wool near the hives. Do not run. Do not shout. They are kinder than most people.
watch: Watch log, day 1. Post manned, three soldiers, fire laid. Road quiet. {weather}. Orders from {place} are to hold until relieved. Standing watch as ever. - {name}
Rations short. Two of the lads sent to {place} for word and not returned. The signal fire is laid but there is no one to see it. We keep the post. It is what we do.
Recall order came today. The garrison is to march at dawn. I am leaving the log, the lamp and {item} for whoever follows. The watch was kept. Let that be written. - {name}, last on the wall.
